findings.issue: Spitter projectiles exist in the sim, the AI, the FX sheet, the config and the anim enum — but have ZERO wire representation. CONTRACT.md gives sim.ts 'spitter projectiles' and zombies.ts 'spitter lob logic'; config.ts has `ranged: true, projectileSpeed: 14`; types.ts has `ZombieAnim = 0|1|2|3; // ... 3 spit-windup`; CONTRACT.md FX sheet demands an 'acid glob (`acid`)'; DESIGN_BIBLE says the Spitter 'stands off and lobs acid'. Yet `t:'snapshot'` carries only `players, zombies, barricades, core, you` — no projectile array — and GameEvent has no spit/impact member. The client can never draw the glob in flight or its impact; the only damage signal is `{t:'dmg_taken'; fromId: PlayerId|null; ...}` where fromId is null for every zombie, so effects.ts also cannot tell acid from a Brute slam. render/effects.ts is contracted to build an asset it can never be told about, and the Spitter's whole 'forces you out of cover' fantasy is invisible.
findings.fix: Before freezing, add to types.ts: `export interface ProjectileSnap { id: number; kind: 'acid'; x: number; y: number; z: number }`, add `projectiles: ProjectileSnap[]` to the snapshot, and add `| { t: 'acid_impact'; x: number; y: number; z: number; radius: number }` plus a source discriminator on player damage — replace `dmg_taken.fromId: PlayerId|null` with `source: { kind: 'zombie'; zombie: ZombieKind } | { kind: 'player'; id: PlayerId } | { kind: 'acid' }` so screen-shake/audio can branch. Add ACID_SPLASH_RADIUS + ACID_ARC_GRAVITY to config.ts.

findings.issue: There is no shared player-movement integrator, yet two modules are separately contracted to produce identical motion. CONTRACT.md gives sim.ts 'player movement (shared physics)' and game.ts 'local prediction (shared physics)', and physics.ts opens with 'The server runs these authoritatively; the client runs the SAME functions for prediction, so they MUST be deterministic'. But the file only exports vadd/vscale/vlen/vnorm/dist2d/resolveCircle/rayAABB/rayWalls/raySphere/headCenter — no step function. Gravity, jump, sprint, air control, ground snap, the perk speed multiplier and the accel/friction model are all left for two different agents in two different workspaces to invent from PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED/PLAYER_GRAVITY/PLAYER_JUMP_SPEED. They will not match, and client-side prediction against a mismatched server step is permanent rubber-banding with no gate that can catch it (there is no test owner either — see the test-ownership finding). Compounding it, nothing builds the collision solid set: walls, `props`, and the state-dependent intact/destroyed barricade boxes must be assembled identically on both sides, and BarricadeDef carries only `{id,x,z,axis}` with no box, width or height.
findings.fix: Freeze in physics.ts: `export interface MoveState { x,y,z,vy: number; grounded: boolean }` and `export function stepPlayer(s: MoveState, moveX: number, moveZ: number, yaw: number, buttons: number, speedMult: number, dt: number, solids: readonly AABB[]): MoveState` — the ONE movement function both sides call. Freeze in map.ts: `export function barricadeBox(d: BarricadeDef): Box` (the 3m gap-spanning solid) and `export function collisionSolids(intactBarricadeIds: readonly number[]): AABB[]`.

findings.issue: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/style.css" />` points at a file that does not exist and that NO module in the CONTRACT.md decomposition owns. The client table lists main/net/game/input, render/*, ui/hud.ts, ui/menus.ts, audio/audio.ts — no CSS owner anywhere. `vite build` (a named gate: 'npm run build') fails on the unresolvable stylesheet, so the very first integration run red-lines with nobody assigned to fix it. Worse, this is not a one-line stub: rift ships a 55KB games/rift/client/src/style.css, and here BOTH ui/hud.ts (crosshair, vitals, wave state, pips, arrows, scoreboard, notifications) and ui/menus.ts (lobby, buy, perk, ammo, end screen, pause) are DOM UIs that need it — so the file is simultaneously owned by nobody and needed by two parallel agents, which is the exact collision the ownership table exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add `client/src/style.css` to the ownership table as a single owner (ui/hud.ts's agent, written FIRST as a frozen CSS-variable + class vocabulary — `--hud-text` etc. mapped from PALETTE, `.op-hud-*` for hud, `.op-menu-*` for menus), and forbid menus.ts from editing it; or split into hud.css + menus.css imported from their respective TS modules and drop the index.html link.

findings.issue: 'npm test (vitest)' is a declared gate but NOT ONE test file is assigned to any of the ~13 implementers. The server table (module/room/sim/zombies/combat/economy/waves) and client table list only production files; 'Integration (orchestrator only)' adds 'vitest.config.ts — add @outpost/shared|server|client aliases + test includes'. Includes pointing at a tree with zero *.test.ts means `npm test` goes green vacuously — the gate reports success while covering nothing. The repo's own vitest.config.ts carries two scar comments about exactly this ('any test written there would have silently never run', 'the PLATFORM had no include at all'), so the failure mode is documented history here. With no unit tests, the pure, cheaply-testable, divergence-critical surfaces — waveBudget/hpScale/pointScale, the economy ledger, parseC2S, resolveCircle/rayAABB, wave-clear and defeat detection — ship unverified behind a browser smoke test that only asserts 'wave + zero console errors'.
findings.fix: Before fan-out, add a test-ownership column: waves.test.ts, economy.test.ts, combat.test.ts, zombies.test.ts, sim.test.ts, room.test.ts (server) and protocol/physics/config-invariant tests (shared), each owned by a DIFFERENT agent than the implementer, dispatched in the same wave against the frozen contract. Make 'its own suite passes' the per-task gate, and add the vitest includes for games/outpost/{shared,server,client}/src/**/*.test.ts to the integration list.

findings.issue: No performance budget exists anywhere in the prep — no target frame time, no draw-call cap, no triangle/memory/bundle ceiling — and the frozen numbers demand a scene the frozen kit cannot draw. `maxAlive(players) => Math.min(24 + players * 8, 160)` allows 160 simultaneous zombies; CONTRACT.md's model sheets budget each at 14–20 prims (shambler/runner/spitter), 18–24 (brute) and 24–36 (abomination), and all of them 'animate: walk / attack / dying via pivot limbs', so kit.ts's `bake()` is explicitly banned for them ('never for animated or per-frame-mutated objects'). That is thousands of draw calls, each rendered again into a PCFSoft 2048 shadow map ('Real-time shadows ON, always ... never disable "for test speed"'). kit.ts offers no InstancedMesh, no LOD, no mesh pool and no dispose path, while RULE 4 orders implementers to 'reuse pools' that do not exist. The renderer will be unusable at 16 players and there is no number in the contract that any agent or gate can fail against.
findings.fix: Add to config.ts: `PERF_TARGET_MS = 16.7`, `MAX_DRAW_CALLS = 180`, `MAX_ZOMBIE_MESH_POOL`, and lower `maxAlive` to ~64. Add to kit.ts before freezing: `makePool<T>(factory, size)`, `bakeAnimated(parts): {root, pivots}` (one merged geometry per limb group so a zombie costs ~5 draws), and an LOD/impostor helper for zombies beyond ~25m. Add a `renderer.info.render.calls` assertion to scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs, mirroring the drawCalls gate splat already uses.

findings.issue: `{ t: 'buy'; weapon: WeaponId } // wall-buy a weapon` carries no station id, and no interaction range or rate exists in config.ts. map.ts explicitly restricts inventory per station — `{ id: 2, x: -12, z: 12, weapons: ['pistol', 'smg'] }` — so the server must know WHICH station the request came from, and it cannot. The same hole covers every other interaction: there is no BUY_RANGE, PERK_RANGE, AMMO_RANGE, REPAIR_RANGE or REPAIR_RATE (hp/sec), and no way to distinguish repair from BARRICADE_REBUILD_COST rebuild — only REVIVE_RANGE/REVIVE_MS exist. economy.ts is ordered to 'read config, never invent constants inline' and then forced to invent all of them. Frozen as-is, either every weapon is buyable from anywhere (BuyStationDef.weapons becomes dead data, the map's economic geography vanishes, and DESIGN_BIBLE's 'hold a breach vs repair vs upgrade' decision collapses) or economy.ts and menus.ts each invent an incompatible proximity rule and the buy menu silently fails.
findings.fix: Change to `{ t: 'buy'; station: number; weapon: WeaponId }` and `{ t: 'buy_ammo'; station: number }`; add `{ t: 'repair'; barricade: number }` / rebuild intent or an explicit interact-target field. Add to config.ts: INTERACT_RANGE, BUY_RANGE, REPAIR_RANGE, REPAIR_HP_PER_SEC, REBUILD_MS. Add `interactKind: 'revive'|'repair'|'rebuild'|'buy'|null`, `interactTargetId: number|null`, `interactProgress: number` to YouSnap so the HUD prompt and hold-bar have a server-authoritative source.

findings.issue: There is no spawn cadence — the single most important pacing number in a wave-defense game is uncontracted. config.ts gives only a total (`waveBudget(wave, players)`) and a concurrency ceiling (`maxAlive`); there is no spawns-per-second, no inter-spawn interval, no per-spawn-point ramp, no boss-entrance delay. waves.ts is handed 'budget/spawn schedule (type unlock + boss cadence), spawning, intermission timing' and must invent the entire tempo curve, so DESIGN_BIBLE's 'Waves ~45–75s each' and 'A run is 15–35 minutes' are unverifiable and unenforceable — a wave could dump all 40 zombies in one tick or trickle them for four minutes and both satisfy the frozen contract. The wave-composition mix is equally absent: ZOMBIE_UNLOCK_WAVE says WHEN a kind first appears and BOSS_EVERY=5 the boss cadence, but nothing says what FRACTION of a wave's budget each unlocked kind takes, so 'Escalation' (pillar 3) has no data behind it.
findings.fix: Add to config.ts before freezing: `SPAWN_INTERVAL_MS(wave)` or `spawnsPerSec(wave, players)`, `BOSS_ENTRANCE_DELAY_MS`, and `waveMix(wave): Record<ZombieKind, number>` returning normalized weights per unlocked kind (with a boss-count rule at BOSS_EVERY). Then DESIGN_BIBLE's 45–75s claim becomes a config-derived assertion a waves.test.ts can check.

findings.issue: The wire type promises a wave timer that config.ts does not define, leaving a hung, unwinnable state with no escape hatch. Snapshot: `phaseEndsAt` — 'serverTime ms the current phase ends (intermission countdown, or wave timeout); 0 when the phase has no timer.' config.ts has INTERMISSION_MS and ENDED_RESET_MS but NO wave timeout, and there is no stuck-entity despawn, no leash and no unreachable-target rule anywhere. waves.ts owns 'wave-clear detection' = zombiesAlive reaches 0. Given BFS nav on a hand-authored map with 3m breach gaps, an abomination of `radius: 1.0` and props scattered outside the walls, one zombie wedged in geometry or pathing to a destroyed-and-rebuilt barricade stalls the wave forever: no clear, no intermission, no respawn for dead players (`respawnAt` is 'next wave start'), no defeat. Every player is locked in a room that can never end, and the e2e gate ('join, start, shoot a zombie, assert wave') never reaches wave 2 so it will not catch it.
findings.fix: Add `WAVE_TIMEOUT_MS` (or a per-zombie `ZOMBIE_STUCK_DESPAWN_MS` + `ZOMBIE_LEASH_RANGE`) to config.ts, and state the rule in CONTRACT.md: on timeout the remaining zombies are force-despawned and the wave counts as cleared (no bonus). Also freeze the defeat rule in the contract, not just in DESIGN_BIBLE prose ('until the core falls or the whole squad is down'), since room.ts and waves.ts both touch it.

findings.issue: Several mandated responsibilities are owned by two modules or by none. (a) Lanterns: scene.ts owns 'lantern pools' while the model sheet gives outpost.ts `makeLantern` — 'post (4 prims): `metalDark` post, `lantern` glass box with `lanternCore` core, warm PointLight falloff' — so both agents will add PointLights (double lighting, blown light budget) or neither will. (b) Hit markers / damage numbers: the client table gives render/effects.ts 'hit markers, damage numbers' while the FX sheet says 'hit marker + floating damage number (HUD)' and ui/hud.ts owns 'notifications' — two owners, one feature. (c) Screen shake: effects.ts owns it but scene.ts owns 'camera', with no seam for who mutates the transform. (d) UX_BIBLE's mandatory 'First-60-seconds onboarding' (5-line overlay + 'look here' arrow at the nearest buy station for 10s), the spectate camera, and 'Subtitles/visual for every audio cue' are owned by NO module — hud.ts's list stops at 'notifications' and menus.ts's at 'pause'. Frozen, those bible requirements simply never get built, and the visual judge loop will report them missing with no one to assign the fix to.
findings.fix: Give lanterns entirely to scene.ts (outpost.ts's makeLantern returns geometry only, zero lights) and state the light budget; move hit markers + damage numbers to ui/hud.ts and strike them from the effects sheet; define screen shake as `effects.shakeOffset(): Vec3` that scene.ts applies. Add explicit owners for the onboarding overlay + buy-station pointer, the spectate camera, and the audio-cue subtitle channel.

findings.issue: kit.ts has no emissive/glow path, so the style bible's central lighting mandate cannot be honored by any art module. `mat()` is declared 'The ONE sanctioned way to get a palette material' and hardcodes `new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({ color: PALETTE[key], flatShading: true })` — no emissive, no emissiveIntensity, no unlit/basic variant. But STYLE_BIBLE requires 'Zombies carry a faint `zeye` emissive so the horde reads in the dark', and CONTRACT.md demands a 'glowing `lanternCore`/`hudAccent` core sphere', a 'small glowing `pointsGold` price sign', a `lanternCore` lantern core, a `lanternCore` perk-station status light, and muzzle/tracer FX — all of which read as dull grey in an unlit dusk scene under a Lambert material with no emissive. RULE 2 ('All colours come from PALETTE via render/kit.ts; ad-hoc hex is a violation') plus the kit header ('none may construct ad-hoc geometry or ad-hoc hex') means implementers cannot legally build their own glow material either. Six art agents will independently hit the same wall and either violate the rule or ship a dark, dead scene.
findings.fix: Add to kit.ts before freezing: `export function glowMat(key: PaletteKey, intensity = 1): THREE.MeshLambertMaterial` (color + emissive from the same palette key, cached separately) and `export function unlitMat(key: PaletteKey): THREE.MeshBasicMaterial` for muzzle flash/tracers/HUD-space sprites, and name them in RULE 2 as the sanctioned glow path.

findings.issue: `place()`'s docstring states an origin convention that its own factories violate: 'Position a mesh at world x/y/z (y = feet) and return it. Origin convention: geometry is centred at its own footprint'. It does `obj.position.set(x, y, z)` on meshes built by makeBox/makeCyl/makeCone — and THREE.BoxGeometry/CylinderGeometry/ConeGeometry are all centred at their CENTROID, not their footprint. CONTRACT.md then repeats the false convention as a global law for every model sheet: 'Origin at footprint centre, ground level, unless noted.' Every one of the six art agents that follows the docs literally (`place(makeBox(2, 3.2, 0.6, 'concrete'), x, 0, z)`) buries half of every wall, crate, station, lantern and zombie limb in the ground — a systematic, scene-wide error that typechecks, passes lint, passes the e2e smoke test, and is only caught by eye in the judge loop, at which point 13 diffs need re-authoring.
findings.fix: Either fix the factories to translate geometry to a footprint origin (`geo.translate(0, h / 2, 0)` inside makeBox/makeCyl/makeCone) and keep the docstring, or keep centre-origin geometry and add `export function placeOnGround<T extends THREE.Object3D>(obj: T, x: number, z: number, height: number): T` plus correct both the kit docstring and CONTRACT.md's 'Origin at footprint centre' line. Do it before freeze — this convention is inherited by every art module.

findings.issue: There is no health recovery of any kind, which bakes in a dominant strategy that inverts a stated design pillar. config.ts has PLAYER_MAX_HP 100, no regen constant, no medkit, no heal purchase; PERKS.juggernaut is '+25 max HP per tier' (raises the ceiling, heals nothing); the only route back to full-ish health is REVIVE_HP = 50 after being downed. Shambler `damage: 20` means five hits across an entire 15–35 minute run. So the optimal play is to deliberately get downed and revived to reclaim HP — free (BLEED_OUT_MS 20s of slack, REVIVE_MS only 2.5s, no point cost) — directly contradicting DESIGN_BIBLE's 'Revive is cheap, death is expensive ... reviving is always the correct instinct' and pillar 1's 'hold the line'. For the solo player (MIN_PLAYERS = 1) there is no reviver at all, so one 100 HP bar must last the 'wave 6–8' target with zero recovery; a single Brute (`damage: 40`) pair-of-hits plus one Spitter glob ends the run regardless of skill.
findings.fix: Add to config.ts: `REGEN_DELAY_MS` + `REGEN_HP_PER_SEC` (out-of-combat regen, the standard fix), or an `armor`/`medkit` purchase with a price that participates in the economy. Then re-derive the solo wave 6–8 target, and add a floor rule so self-downing is strictly worse than staying up (e.g. revive restores REVIVE_HP only if current HP < REVIVE_HP, and each down raises the next bleed-out penalty).

findings.issue: The economy runs away rather than running out, so DESIGN_BIBLE's stated loss driver does not exist and the intermission decision dies by mid-run. Total lifetime spend is bounded: weapons 1000+1500+2500+4000 = 9,000, perks 9,500+6,500+6,500+12,000 = 34,500 → 43,500 points, and YouSnap.weapons has no carry limit (no MAX_WEAPONS constant) so a player simply owns all five. Income is unbounded and scales faster than costs: `POINTS_PER_DMG = 0.2` on hp that grows 8%/wave (`hpScale`) PLUS killPoints on `pointScale` (5%/wave) PLUS `WAVE_CLEAR_BONUS 100` + wave*20. After saturation the only sinks left are ammo at `AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND = 1` (a full 300-round LMG reserve costs 300 points — roughly three shambler kills) and barricade repair at 1 hp/point. So 'Points are scarce and single-currency. Every minute the player chooses: hold a breach vs repair vs upgrade' is false from roughly wave 12 onward, and '~wave 18–20 before the economy can't keep up' describes a failure mode the numbers cannot produce — the actual wall is linear, unbounded `hpScale` against a fixed damage ceiling, i.e. an infinite grind with no defeat pressure.
findings.fix: Add a carry limit (`MAX_WEAPONS = 2`, forcing a real loadout decision), scale the sinks with the wave (`ammoCost(weapon, wave)`, `repairCost(wave)`, `rebuildCost(wave)`), and add a late-game sink (weapon upgrade tiers / core reinforcement). Then restate the DESIGN_BIBLE line as a checkable relationship against the real functions, and let waves.test.ts assert income-vs-cost at waves 1/6/12/20.

findings.issue: The scoreboard the design is built around is never updated on the wire. `RosterEntry` (kills, headshots, revives, downs, points) is delivered only in `t:'joined'` (`roster: RosterEntry[]`) and in `{ t: 'player_joined'; entry: RosterEntry }` — snapshots carry no roster and no scores array, and there is no periodic roster event. ui/hud.ts owns 'scoreboard' and UX_BIBLE binds Tab to it, while DESIGN_BIBLE pillar 2 makes it load-bearing: 'a scoreboard that rewards revives and headshots, not just raw kills'. A client can only reconstruct it by tallying broadcast events it happened to witness, so anyone who joins mid-match, reconnects, or drops a packet shows a permanently wrong board — and `MatchStat.damage` is not derivable from any broadcast event at all. The same one-shot problem hits the `ended` state: `{t:'match_end'; stats}` is a single event, but `ended` is a required UX state that a reloading or late-joining client can enter with no stats to render.
findings.fix: Add `roster: readonly RosterEntry[]` to the snapshot (or a `{t:'scores'; roster}` broadcast on every kill/revive and wave boundary), add `damage` to RosterEntry, and add `endStats: readonly MatchStat[] | null` to the `joined` payload so a client entering during `ended` can draw the stats screen.

findings.issue: Action states the HUD, viewmodel and teammate renderer must show are absent from both snapshot structs. YouSnap has `mag`/`reserve` but no `reloading`/`reloadEndsAt`, no `adsActive`, no `fireReadyAt`; PlayerSnap has `yaw/pitch/hp/alive/downed/weapon/perks` but no `reloading`, `firing`, `sprinting` or `interacting`. render/viewmodel.ts is contracted for 'recoil/reload animation' and render/players.ts for 'Teammate bodies + downed pose + revive indicator', and neither has a source of truth: teammates will stand idle while shooting, and a client-only reload animation desyncs from the server the moment a reload is cancelled by a `switch` (PERKS.quickload's '+25% reload speed per tier' makes the client-side guess wrong in a second way). UX_BIBLE's 'Action → on-screen response ≤ 50ms' and 'E interact (hold for revive/repair)' hold-progress have no wire signal at all, and the 2.5s revive hold-bar cannot be drawn authoritatively.
findings.fix: Add to YouSnap: `reloadEndsAt: number`, `ads: boolean`, `interactProgress: number`, `interactKind: 'revive'|'repair'|'rebuild'|null`. Add to PlayerSnap a compact `flags: number` bitfield (FIRING/RELOADING/SPRINTING/ADS/INTERACTING) with exported FLAG_* constants alongside the INPUT_* block.

findings.issue: `@outpost/shared` exports a `RoomInfo` that shadows the platform's `RoomInfo`, and the client imports both barrels. outpost's is `{ id, code, players, maxPlayers, phase: Phase, visibility }`; platform/shared/src/module.ts's — the one `GameRoomHandle.info()` must actually return — is `{ id, code, game: string, label: string, players, maxPlayers, phase: string, visibility }`. index.ts does `export * from './types.js'`, so `import type { RoomInfo } from '@outpost/shared'` compiles and silently yields the wrong shape; net.ts and menus.ts (lobby list) are exactly the modules that will reach for it. The outpost variant is used by nothing — `room_list` is lobby-owned, and types.ts itself says so ('`welcome`, `room_list` and `pong` are LOBBY-owned') — so it is a dead type whose only effect is to mislead. Related smaller trap in the same surface: `YouSnap.weapons: readonly WeaponId[] // owned, current first` reorders on every weapon switch while UX_BIBLE binds '1–5 weapon switch' to stable slots, so the hotkeys point at a different gun after each swap.
findings.fix: Delete outpost's `RoomInfo` (or rename it `OutpostRoomInfo` and mark it internal), and change YouSnap to `weapons: readonly WeaponId[] // owned, in WEAPON_ORDER — stable slot order for the 1–5 hotkeys` with `weapon` alone carrying 'currently held'.

findings.issue: The hitbox model is half-specified, so combat.ts must invent the constants config.ts forbids it to invent. `headCenter(feetY, scale)` returns only a Y coordinate ('Head sphere centre for a zombie (y above feet)'), and `raySphere(r, cx, cy, cz, radius)` demands a radius that nothing defines — there is no HEAD_RADIUS, no body-sphere/capsule dimensions, and ZombieDef's `radius` is documented as 'collision/hit sphere radius' doing double duty for movement collision and bullet hits. Headshots are a load-bearing mechanic (WeaponDef.headshotMult 1.5–2.5, ZombieDef.headshotBonus, DESIGN_BIBLE 'Headshots pay ... the skill ceiling is rewarded'), and its hitbox size is unfrozen. combat.ts also owns 'Lag-compensated hitscan' with no lag-comp window, no snapshot-history depth and no max rewind in config, so the rewind budget is invented too — and the shotgun (`pellets: 8`) has no per-pellet spread pattern or seeding rule, so client tracers and server hits will diverge visibly.
findings.fix: Add to config.ts: `HEAD_RADIUS_MULT` (or per-kind headRadius on ZombieDef), `BODY_HIT_RADIUS_MULT`, `PLAYER_HEAD_RADIUS`, `LAG_COMP_MAX_MS`, `SNAPSHOT_HISTORY_TICKS`, `PELLET_SEED_MODE`. Add a shared `pelletDirs(yaw, pitch, weapon, seq): Vec3[]` to physics.ts so client FX and server hit resolution use one deterministic spread.

findings.issue: The model sheets name palette keys that do not exist, in a document whose own RULE 2 makes that unbuildable. `makeBuyStation` calls for '2–3 weapon silhouettes in `steel`-ish tones' — palette.ts has no `steel` (only metalDark/metalDeep) — and `makeAmmoCrate` calls for a '`hazardAmber`-like stencil (use `hudAccent`)', naming a key that does not exist and patching it inline. RULE 2 says 'All colours come from `PALETTE` via `render/kit.ts`; ad-hoc hex is a violation' and kit.ts's `mat(key: PaletteKey)` is compile-enforced against `keyof typeof PALETTE`, so `mat('steel')` is a type error and the implementer must either guess a substitute or stop. In the other direction, `fire: '#ff8e16'` and `concreteDark` are in the frozen palette but assigned to no asset or module — dead entries that signal a missing FX (there is no fire/explosion anywhere in the FX sheet, DESIGN_BIBLE or GameEvent list).
findings.fix: Search-and-replace the model sheets to real keys (`steel` → `metalDark`/`concreteLit`, `hazardAmber` → `hudAccent`), and either assign `fire` and `concreteDark` to a named asset (e.g. core-damage flame, secondary wall plane) or delete them from palette.ts before freeze.

findings.issue: The world-population mandate requires a colour family the frozen palette deliberately withholds. CONTRACT.md: 'render/terrain.ts — Ground (ash/mud), rubble/vegetation population' and '~40 rubble piles / crates / broken pallets ... 8–12 dead trees or antenna stubs outside the walls'. palette.ts's only greens are the enemy family, and both the palette header and STYLE_BIBLE make their exclusivity the foundation of the whole look: 'zombies as the single saturated sickly-green "enemy" family that pops from every surface (the readability rule)' / 'The one saturated family is the zombie ramp'. So terrain.ts's agent has exactly two legal moves: reuse `zskin`/`zskinDark` for vegetation and destroy the readability rule the art direction rests on (green scrub reading as a distant zombie at gameplay range is the specific failure), or ship no vegetation and under-deliver the 'lived-in BEFORE the horde arrives, not an empty plane' brief. Secondary gap in the same mandate: STYLE_BIBLE requires 'Every wall base and prop base wears its `…Deep` contact band', but the perk station's `charcoal` body and the survivor family have no `…Deep` counterpart.
findings.fix: Either strike 'vegetation' from the terrain brief (dead trees + rubble only, `woodDark`/`woodDeep`/`rock`/`rockDeep`) or add two desaturated, low-chroma entries far from the zskin hue — e.g. `driedGrass: '#6a6141'`, `driedGrassDeep: '#403a26'` — and state in STYLE_BIBLE that world greens are always desaturated and never emissive. Add `charcoalDeep` and `survivorDeep` so the contact-band rule is satisfiable everywhere it is mandated.

findings.issue: The aesthetic gate is named but not specified. Gates read: 'node scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs (headless browser: join, start, shoot a zombie, assert wave + zero console errors) · screenshot judge loop (Phase 4)'. The functional half is genuinely sound — it runs the game AND asserts. The aesthetic half is a phase label with no rubric, no per-aspect judge list, no pass threshold, no capture manifest (which camera angles, which wave, dusk vs lantern-lit), no iteration cap, and — most damaging — no named shipped title for the blind side-by-side. STYLE_BIBLE lists touchstones ('STRICKEN ... Left 4 Dead ... CoD Zombies, stylized low-poly') but a flat-shaded Lambert browser game judged blind against Left 4 Dead's render class loses on lighting model alone, no matter how good the craft is; the benchmark has to match the render class or the loop never terminates. The e2e also asserts nothing about draw calls or frame time (see the perf finding), and never reaches wave 2, so wave transition, intermission, buy, downed/revive and defeat are all ungated.
findings.fix: Before freeze, write judge/RUBRIC.md: the per-aspect judge list (silhouette/lighting/materials/FX/HUD/composition), a numeric pass bar, an explicit capture manifest, an iteration cap, and a named flat-shaded/stylized comparison title in the SAME render class. Extend scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs with `settings.speed` to drive wave 1 → clear → intermission → buy → wave 2, and assert `renderer.info.render.calls` under MAX_DRAW_CALLS.

findings.issue: The RULES block carries bake, pool and no-hot-alloc but is missing the capability and lifecycle guards. RULE 4 covers 'Bake/merge static geometry; no per-frame allocation in hot paths; reuse pools' and RULE 5 covers 'One throw must never white-screen', but there is no WebGL2-unavailable / context-lost guard, no reduced-motion or reduced-quality path, no tab-blur/visibilitychange rule (a rAF client predicting through a backgrounded tab against a 20 Hz server rubber-bands hard on return, and audio.ts's WebAudio graph keeps running), and no resize/DPR-change discipline beyond STYLE_BIBLE's 'pixel ratio capped at 1.5' — which no RULE or module is told to enforce or re-apply on a monitor change. There is also no dispose/teardown protocol: kit.ts's `bake()` clones and merges geometry and disposes only the clones, so every source BoxGeometry from makeBox leaks, and nothing owns tearing the scene down between matches (`ended` → `lobby` after ENDED_RESET_MS rebuilds the world). No memory or bundle ceiling is stated anywhere.
findings.fix: Add RULES 10–13: (10) capability-guard — probe WebGL2 and handle webglcontextlost with a visible message, never a white screen; (11) pause prediction/audio on visibilitychange and resnap from the next snapshot; (12) clamp devicePixelRatio to 1.5 on every resize and on DPR change, debounced; (13) every render module exports `dispose()` and the scene is torn down on match reset. Fix `bake()` to dispose source geometries, and add MAX_BUNDLE_KB to the gates.

findings.issue: `bake()`'s docstring contradicts its code and it fails silently. The doc says it 'Returns a single Mesh when all share one material, else a Group of per-material merged meshes', but every path builds `const out = new THREE.Group()` and returns it — a caller that trusts the doc and does `(bake(meshes) as THREE.Mesh).geometry` gets undefined, and `as` casts to reconcile it are banned by RULE 8. Separately, `const merged = mergeGeometries(geoms); if (merged) { ... }` drops an entire material group with no warning when mergeGeometries returns null (mismatched attribute sets), so an art module can lose a third of its geometry and see a clean console — which the e2e gate's only visual assertion is 'zero console errors'.
findings.fix: Correct the docstring to 'always returns a Group of per-material merged meshes' (or implement the single-Mesh fast path), and make the null branch `console.warn` + throw in dev so the loss is visible to the gate rather than silent.

findings.issue: The 'Balance as relationships (checkable, not vibes)' section is not checkable against the frozen numbers. 'Wood-positive: wave-1 clear (~8 zombies × ~150 pts + 100 bonus ≈ 1300 pts) buys the SMG before wave 3' — but `waveBudget(1, 1) = Math.min(8 + 1*3 + 1*3, 40 + 6) = 14`, not 8; a shambler pays `POINTS_PER_DMG(0.2) * hp(100) + killPoints(60) = 80`, not ~150 (120 with the headshot bonus); and the bonus is `WAVE_CLEAR_BONUS 100 + wave*20 = 120`, not 100. Every operand in the one worked example is wrong, and the total lands near 1300 only by cancellation. The 'Zombie personality' section has the same problem in the other direction: 'Brute — tears barricades and knocks players back' and 'Abomination — a siege engine that walks through barricades' name behaviours with no config field (no knockback force/duration, no barricade-phasing flag), and 'Runner — flanks' names an AI behaviour with no parameter, so zombies.ts must invent all three.
findings.fix: Recompute the example from the frozen functions and state it as `waveBudget(1,1)=14 × 80 + 120 = 1240 ≥ WEAPONS.smg.price` so a waves.test.ts can assert it. Add `knockback: number` and `phasesBarricades: boolean` to ZombieDef (0/false for the other four kinds), and a `flankBias: number`, so the personality prose maps to config.

findings.issue: The solo wave-1 ammo budget has near-zero margin, which the 'warm-up' framing does not acknowledge. `waveBudget(1,1) = 14` shamblers × `hp 100` = 1400 hp; the starting pistol is `damage: 20, magSize: 12, reserveMax: 72` = 84 rounds total = 1680 damage on a 100% body-shot hit rate, i.e. a 14-round margin before a new player is dry. DESIGN_BIBLE frames waves 1–3 as 'a warm-up (Shamblers only) so new players learn shooting', but a new player missing ~20% of shots runs out mid-wave and must break contact for an ammo crate (`ammoCrates: [{x:-8,z:0},{x:8,z:0}]`) — survivable, since `POINTS_PER_DMG 0.2` yields ~280 points during the wave and `AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND = 1`, but it is the opposite of a warm-up and it is not stated anywhere, so waves.ts and economy.ts will not know it is intentional.
findings.fix: Either raise pistol reserveMax to ~120 or drop shambler hp for waves 1–2 via a warm-up clause in hpScale, and state the intended wave-1 ammo margin in DESIGN_BIBLE as a checkable relationship (rounds available vs wave HP) that waves.test.ts asserts.
